variants.title: Payments hang every checkout
variants.context: The payment provider is down and every checkout thread waits 30 seconds.
variants.constraint: The rest of the site could still browse.
variants.question: What stops the thread pileup?
variants.expectedPattern: Open a circuit after consecutive failures and fail fast instead of waiting on the timeout.

variants.title: Retrying a dead dependency
variants.context: An inventory service returns 503 and callers retry three times, tripling load.
variants.constraint: The dependency needs time to recover.
variants.question: What should happen after the error budget is spent?
variants.expectedPattern: Trip the breaker, stop calling for a cooldown, then probe with limited traffic.

variants.title: Partial outage looks healthy
variants.context: 1 in 3 calls fail, but the breaker never opens because it only trips on 100% failure.
variants.question: What trip condition is better?
variants.expectedPattern: Open on error rate or latency SLO breach, not only total blackout.
wrongChoices: Trip only if every call fails

variants.title: Breaker never half-opens
variants.context: A circuit opened at 02:00 and still rejects all calls at noon even though the dependency recovered at 02:10.
variants.question: What state is missing?
variants.expectedPattern: Half-open: allow a small probe, then close the circuit if the dependency is healthy.
wrongChoices: Stay open forever until a restart
Close immediately on the first timeout
Page a human for every recovery

variants.title: One slow endpoint poisons the client
variants.context: A shared HTTP client trips for all routes because /reports is slow.
variants.question: How should breakers be scoped?
variants.expectedPattern: Per-dependency and per-endpoint circuits, not one breaker for the whole host.
wrongChoices: One global breaker for every outbound call

variants.title: Fallback to stale catalog
variants.context: The recommendations service is down and the homepage waits on it.
variants.constraint: A slightly stale list is acceptable.
variants.question: What should the open circuit return?
variants.expectedPattern: A fallback: cached or default recommendations instead of blocking the page.
wrongChoices: Write a full outage banner for unrelated pages

variants.title: Breaker on the database
variants.context: Postgres is slow and every request still opens a new query.
variants.constraint: Holding more connections makes recovery worse.
variants.question: What does a circuit do here?
variants.expectedPattern: Fail fast when the database error rate is high so the pool can recover.
wrongChoices: Retry every query with no delay

variants.title: Flapping circuit
variants.context: The breaker opens and closes every few seconds as one probe succeeds then fails.
variants.question: How do you stabilize it?
variants.expectedPattern: Require a streak of successful probes and a minimum open duration before closing.

variants.title: Timeout longer than user patience
variants.context: The user abandons at 3s, but the service waits 30s on a vendor API.
variants.constraint: Resources stay occupied after the user is gone.
variants.question: What bound belongs with the breaker?
variants.expectedPattern: Timeouts shorter than the user SLA, then trip if those timeouts become common.
wrongChoices: Vendor timeout of 30s on the user path

variants.title: Bulkhead missing next to the breaker
variants.context: A circuit opens on search, but search still occupies the only thread pool.
variants.question: What complementary pattern is needed?
variants.expectedPattern: Isolate thread pools (bulkhead) so a broken dependency cannot starve others, then break the circuit.
wrongChoices: One thread pool for every outbound call

variants.title: Error budget vs pager
variants.context: On-call is paged for every 500, but the circuit already sheds 99% of calls cleanly.
variants.question: What should alerting follow?
variants.expectedPattern: Alert on customer impact and breaker state, not every expected fail-fast 503.
wrongChoices: Treat fail-fast as an unknown outage every time

variants.title: Idempotent probe in half-open
variants.context: Half-open sends a real purchase to see if payments are back.
variants.constraint: Probes must not create side effects.
variants.question: What kind of probe is safe?
variants.expectedPattern: A health or dry-run call, not a live mutating request, while half-open.
wrongChoices: Charge a real card as the probe
Send production writes with no idempotency key

variants.title: Shared library default is closed-never
variants.context: The HTTP wrapper has retries but no circuit, so a brownout lasts all afternoon.
variants.question: What default should the platform provide?
variants.expectedPattern: Timeouts, limited retries, and a circuit breaker as the standard client policy.
wrongChoices: Infinite retries as the SDK default
No timeouts in the shared client
Each team invents a different policy with no breaker

variants.title: gRPC deadline ignored
variants.context: Downstream ignores deadlines and the caller’s breaker never sees failures, only hung RPCs.
variants.question: What failure signal should trip the circuit?
variants.expectedPattern: Treat deadline exceeded and hung RPCs as failures that count toward opening the circuit.

variants.title: Regional dependency, global breaker
variants.context: EU payments fail, so the breaker opens for US traffic too.
variants.question: How should circuits be partitioned?
variants.expectedPattern: Per-region or per-cluster breakers so a local outage does not fail other regions.
wrongChoices: One global circuit for all geos
Close EU and US together always
Route EU users to a dead US dependency without a breaker
